ai.title: Clean up background processes on start
ai.summary: Added `cleanupStoredProcesses` to `index.ts` to kill orphaned background processes on CLI startup. Implemented `spawnAndTrack` and `killAllBackgroundProcesses` in `background-process-manager.ts` using PID files in `CONFIG_DIR/background_processes`. Updated `cli.ts` exit handlers to await async cleanup and `dev-process-manager.ts` to log process IDs on successful start.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant’s tool, it now quietly checks for any leftover background tasks from a previous session and shuts them down before beginning. This prevents stray processes from piling up over time. You wouldn’t see a new button or setting for it, but the system should feel a bit cleaner each time it starts.

ai.title: Fix OpenAI stopsequences param handling for o3 and o4mini
ai.summary: Updated `openai-api.ts` to map `stop_sequences` to the `stop` parameter, with conditional logic for `o3` and `o4mini` models. In `promptOpenAIStream`, `stop` is set to `undefined` for these models, while in `promptOpenAIWithContinuation`, it receives the `stopSequences` value. This ensures correct parameter passing across different streaming methods.

eli5.text: When talking to OpenAI's newer o3 and o4mini assistant models, the system now handles the 'stop sequences' setting correctly. Depending on which streaming method is used, it either passes the stop sequences through to the model or leaves them out entirely for these specific models. This prevents a parameter conflict that could cause errors during conversations with these newer models.

ai.title: Add timeout and error logging to fetchStoredAPIKeyTypes
ai.summary: Added a 5-second timeout to `fetchStoredAPIKeyTypes` in `npm-app/src/client.ts` using `Promise.race`. Non-production environments now log fetch errors, specifically flagging port 3000 conflicts.

eli5.text: Developers working on this project's internal tools will now see clearer error messages if a request to load API key types hangs or fails in development and staging environments. Behind the scenes, the system now gives up on that request after five seconds instead of waiting indefinitely, and it logs a specific note suggesting a possible conflict on the local development port when the failure happens. The change is in place for internal tooling only and does not affect live end users today.

ai.title: Log auto top-up success in client
ai.summary: Added console logging for successful automatic credit top-ups in `npm-app/src/client.ts`. The client now checks `pendingTopUpMessageAmount` after request processing and prints a green success message with the added credit count before clearing the state. This change affects the CLI client's output stream.

eli5.text: When the tool automatically adds more credits to your account after they run low, it now shows you a success confirm in your terminal window instead of doing it quietly. You would see a highlighted message telling you how many credits were added, then the system forgets about that pending addition so it doesn't show the message again. This only affects people using the command-line version of the app.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.225
ai.summary: Package version incremented to 1.0.225 in npm-app/package.json. Routine release preparation for the codebuff CLI.

eli5.text: Updating to the new version of the assistant will clear out leftover background processes that may have been running from earlier sessions. This prevents stale tasks from interfering with new work. The update also improves reliability when checking for stored API keys and logging automatic credit top-ups. These improvements are live now for anyone who updates to the latest version.

ai.title: Balance settlement logic and net display
ai.summary: Billing middleware now performs in-memory settlement of debt against positive balances before calculating net balance, replacing the previous hard block on any debt. The usage display component exposes `netBalance` with conditional red styling for negative values and updated tooltip text. Scope includes `balance-calculator.ts` for core logic, `billing.knowledge.md` for documentation, and web API/UI files for presentation. Consumption logic no longer throws on existing debt, relying instead on net balance checks.

eli5.text: The system no longer blocks your account from using services the moment you have any money you've borrowed (like a past-due amount). Instead, it looks at your overall balance: if you have enough positive credit to cover what you owe, you're still allowed to use it. If you don't, you'll see your total shown in red with a note explaining the amount still owed after your existing credit is applied. This applies whether you're logged in or checking your usage online.
